title: Central African Empire
capsule: The Central African Empire (Empire Centrafricain) was proclaimed on 4 December 1976 when Jean-Bédel Bokassa, president of the Central African Republic since his 1966 coup, declared himself Emperor Bokassa I and staged an extravagant coronation in December 1977 modeled on Napoleon's, at a cost estimated at $30 million — roughly one third of the country's annual budget. Bokassa's regime was characterized by personal brutality: in April 1979 security forces, with his direct participation, massacred schoolchildren who had protested a decree requiring expensive uniforms. France, the former colonial power and continuing patron, intervened militarily in Operation Barracuda on 20 September 1979, restoring former president David Dacko and ending the empire after less than four years.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Central African Empire was coterminous with the Central African Republic's internationally recognized territory; its boundaries are unambiguous and well documented.
